name: Analytical Thinking
definition: Interprets numerical information and data accurately, and uses it as a foundation for decisions. Spots patterns and anomalies in data, and is honest about what the numbers do and do not actually support. Grounds arguments in evidence the data can carry, and pushes back when others draw conclusions the numbers do not support.
high: Builds conclusions from the underlying data rather than from someone else's summary; names where the numbers stop supporting the argument rather than overreaching.
low: Takes summary numbers at face value without checking how they were built; draws conclusions the data does not actually support.

name: Commercial Acumen
definition: Understands how the business actually makes and protects money, and uses that understanding to shape decisions. Reads commercial signals like margin, cost, market shifts, and competitive moves, and translates them into implications for current choices. Weighs commercial impact of decisions explicitly, rather than treating financial consequence as someone else's department.
high: Names the cost, revenue, and competitive implications of proposed decisions before signing off; reads market signals and adjusts before they show up in the numbers.
low: Treats decisions as functional rather than commercial; defers cost and revenue questions to "the business side" rather than weighing them in own choices.

name: Critical Analysis (Evaluation)
definition: Breaks complex problems and information into components to identify causes, evidence, and what actually matters. Distinguishes symptoms from root causes, weighs the quality of evidence, and tests competing explanations against the data before settling on a conclusion. Drives to root causes rather than stopping at the first plausible explanation that fits.
high: Strips complex problems into components and tests competing explanations against the evidence before concluding; pushes others past surface answers to root causes.
low: Jumps from problem to solution without testing the reasoning; accepts the first plausible explanation that fits without checking the evidence.

name: Ingenuity
definition: Generates original solutions to problems where conventional answers do not fit. Combines knowledge from different fields, takes calculated risks on unproven ideas, and pushes past the obvious next step to find something better. Moves novel ideas through to implementation, not just generation, so creative insight actually changes how the work gets done.
high: Proposes solutions outside the obvious answer set by combining ideas from different fields; champions novel approaches through scepticism rather than abandoning them at the first pushback.
low: Defaults to established methods even when they no longer fit the problem; lets unconventional ideas die in committee rather than building the case to push them through.

name: Judgement
definition: Makes sound decisions with the information available, even when the picture is incomplete or the timing is tight. Weighs logic, data, experience, and risk together, and is willing to commit to a call rather than wait for certainty that will not come. Matches confidence to the evidence, willing to back a call hard when warranted and willing to revise when new information warrants it.
high: Decides at the point where additional information would not change the call; explicitly names risk and matches own confidence to the evidence at hand.
low: Delays decisions while waiting for information that will not arrive; defaults to precedent or escalates rather than exercising own judgement.

name: Strategic Vision
definition: Takes a long-term view that runs in years and decades, not quarters. Integrates market signals, competitive moves, and longer-term shifts into a coherent direction for the business or team. Tests current decisions against where the business needs to be in three to five years, rather than only against this quarter's targets.
high: Tests current decisions against where the business needs to be in three to five years; names the strategic implication when others stop at the day-to-day.
low: Optimises for this quarter's targets without weighing longer-term implications; reacts to market shifts after they become obvious rather than anticipating them.

name: Decision Prioritisation
definition: Allocates own and the team's attention to the decisions that will have the most impact, and de-prioritises or delegates the rest. Distinguishes urgent from important, settles low-value choices fast so they do not crowd out high-value ones, and revisits priorities as conditions change. Treats own attention as a finite resource to be invested where it matters, not a default response to whoever asks last.
high: Names the one or two decisions that matter most this week and protects attention for them; settles or delegates low-value choices fast so they do not crowd out the work that matters.
low: Responds to incoming demands in the order they arrive rather than the order of their impact; lets urgent low-value work crowd out important work.

name: Execution (Implementation)
definition: Delivers what they said they would, when they said they would, to the quality they said. Maintains focus on the current task without getting pulled by competing demands or shiny new work. Treats commitments as firm rather than flexible, so colleagues can plan around what they say they will do.
high: Closes loops on committed work without being chased; flags slippage early enough that others can adjust rather than absorb the consequence.
low: Gets pulled to new work before closing the old; negotiates commitments down rather than meeting them, or flags slippage only when it is already late.

name: Organisation
definition: Translates goals into structured, realistic plans with clear milestones, owners, and timing. Anticipates obstacles, accounts for dependencies, and builds plans that hold up when conditions shift rather than collapse at the first surprise. Plans at the level of detail the work actually needs, neither over-engineering simple work nor under-planning complex work.
high: Sets out clear milestones, owners, and dependencies before work begins; adapts the plan when conditions shift without abandoning the structure.
low: Starts work without naming milestones or dependencies; treats slipping deadlines as routine rather than as a planning failure to learn from.

name: Performance Tenacity
definition: Pursues goals through repeated rejection, slow progress, or extended cycles without losing momentum. Adapts approach based on what is and is not working, while continuing to advance toward the same objective rather than abandoning it. Knows when continued effort is worth it and when to redirect, rather than either giving up too early or chasing a goal that's no longer worth it.
high: Returns to high-value opportunities after rejection with an adapted approach; sustains effort and energy across cycles long enough to convert what others abandon.
low: Drops opportunities after the first rejection or extended slow patch; lets pipeline or pursuits thin out rather than reworking the approach.

name: Process Discipline
definition: Applies policies, procedures, and ethical standards consistently, including when corners would be easier to cut. Raises concerns when processes are being bypassed by others, rather than letting it pass for the sake of expediency. Combines compliance with practical judgement, knowing when a process needs to be followed strictly and when escalation is the right move.
high: Follows the process even when shortcuts would be easier and faster; raises it when others bypass procedures rather than letting it pass for expediency.
low: Cuts corners under deadline or workload pressure; lets others' shortcuts go unflagged so long as the output looks acceptable.

name: Building Relationships
definition: Establishes and sustains productive working relationships across levels, functions, and time. Creates warmth and trust quickly in new relationships, and invests effort in keeping connections alive between transactions and across role changes. Treats relationships as ongoing rather than as means to a current end, so the connection itself is the work, not just the outcome it produces.
high: Reaches out to people without a current ask and invests in trust before it is needed; remembered positively by people they no longer work with.
low: Contacts colleagues only when there is something to gain from the conversation; lets relationships lapse the moment the current task ends.

name: Collaboration (Teamwork)
definition: Contributes fully to joint work, sharing information, delivering on commitments, and supporting others to do the same. Reads team dynamics and actively manages the conditions for the group to succeed, surfacing tensions, bridging differences, and lifting morale. Puts the team's outcome ahead of personal credit or individual standing.
high: Shares information and bridges differences in the team before being asked; gives credit publicly for joint work even when their own contribution is large.
low: Holds information close that would help colleagues; lets tensions in the team grow rather than surface them.

name: Communication
definition: Conveys ideas with clarity, structure, and economy across written and verbal channels. Adapts register, detail level, and medium to fit the audience and the moment, and listens as actively as they speak. Aims for the audience landing the message, not for the elegance of the delivery.
high: Adapts language, structure, and detail level to the specific audience and the moment; tests for understanding rather than assuming the message has landed.
low: Uses one style and level of detail across boards, peers, and frontline teams; gives the audience more than they can hold at once.

name: Influence (Negotiation)
definition: Moves others toward agreement by understanding their underlying needs and crafting paths between competing positions. Reads the room and adjusts approach in real time, knowing when to push, when to concede, and when to walk away. Preserves the working relationship through disagreement rather than winning at its expense.
high: Walks into negotiations having mapped the other party's underlying needs and constraints; adjusts tactic mid-conversation based on what the room is showing.
low: Argues from own position without understanding what the other party actually needs; damages the working relationship in pursuit of the deal.

name: Interpersonal Sensitivity
definition: Reads other people's emotional and social signals accurately as they happen, picking up on tone, body language, and what is left unsaid as much as what is said. Adjusts approach in real time based on what the other person is showing, rather than continuing with a prepared script. Stays outwardly focused on understanding the other person, not on managing own image or delivering a message.
high: Picks up on what is not being said and adjusts tone or approach mid-conversation; names the unspoken thing in the room when it matters.
low: Continues with prepared message when the room has shifted; gets blindsided by relational fallout from interactions they thought went well.

name: Achievement Drive
definition: Brings sustained energy and ambition to goals, including ones that are demanding or competitive. Sets and seeks demanding targets rather than comfortable ones, and stays engaged when the work is hard or progress is slow. Pushes for more than what was asked for, treating the bar as a starting point rather than a finishing line.
high: Volunteers for stretch targets rather than comfortable ones; sustains energy and intensity when others are flagging or progress is slow.
low: Accepts targets at the level offered without pushing for more; energy drops when work becomes slow, repetitive, or non-competitive.

name: Emotional Regulation
definition: Manages own emotional responses in real time, especially under stress, conflict, or ambiguity. Recognises emotional triggers as they fire and selects a measured response rather than reacting on impulse, withdrawing, or freezing. Keeps composure visible in heated moments, with reactions not leaking into tone, pace, or body language.
high: Pauses before responding when emotions rise; tone, pace and body language hold under heat.
low: Reacts within seconds when emotions rise; carries the feeling into the next conversation or meeting.

name: Flexibility
definition: Adjusts approach, plans, and methods readily when circumstances change. Treats new direction or shifting priorities as a working condition rather than a disruption that requires recovery time. Re-orients quickly even when change is unwelcome or imposed, and helps colleagues through the transition rather than slowing it down.
high: Switches plans mid-execution when new information lands; carries imposed change to the team without venting.
low: Re-opens decisions after they're settled; defaults to familiar approaches even when they're not working.

name: Learning Agility
definition: Absorbs new information, methods, and concepts rapidly and applies them to unfamiliar problems. Looks for the principles behind things rather than just the surface, and transfers what they learn into the next situation rather than treating each as new. Seeks out unfamiliar territory rather than relying on what they already know, and treats being wrong as the fastest route to learning.
high: Volunteers for unfamiliar problems and looks for the underlying principle so it transfers to the next; tests own mental models against new evidence rather than defending them.
low: Sticks to familiar approaches even when they no longer fit the problem; treats each new situation as new rather than connecting it to what they already know.

name: Resilience
definition: Recovers quickly from setbacks, criticism, and prolonged pressure without sustained drop in performance. Sustains output and energy through extended stress without showing wear in tone, pace, or quality. Reframes adversity as something to absorb and move past rather than dwell on or spiral into worst-case thinking.
high: Re-engages with the work within hours of a setback; sustains output and tone through extended pressure.
low: Brings up past failures emotionally long after the moment; scales back ambition after public mistakes.

name: Self-Insight
definition: Reads own strengths, gaps, and how behaviour lands on others accurately, matching how peers and reports would describe them. Takes in feedback without filtering or dismissing it, including the parts that are uncomfortable. Can name and discuss specific habits and tendencies in own behaviour, not just sense them privately.
high: Talks about own patterns and gaps in specific terms peers would recognise; acknowledges own role in difficulties before being asked.
low: Repeats the same patterns after multiple rounds of feedback; blames circumstances or others when own performance is questioned.

name: Visible Self-Development
definition: Actively tells people what they are working on and asks for feedback on it regularly. Sets development as a public commitment to manager, peers, or coach, in language they can repeat back and check on. Returns to those people to update progress, including setbacks, rather than developing in private.
high: Names current development priorities and accountability partners on demand; returns to those people to update on progress and setbacks.
low: Works on gaps privately without telling anyone what they're working on; waits for the manager to raise development in performance conversations.

name: Decisive Leadership (Directing Action)
definition: Sets clear direction for the team, makes the call when the team needs one, and owns the consequences. Delegates the work to the right people with the right authority, and holds people accountable to what they signed up for. Backs people to own their work rather than reaching down into it, while making clear what they will be accountable for.
high: Names the call when the team is stuck and owns the consequences publicly; delegates work with clear authority and lets people own it without reaching back in.
low: Waits for consensus or escalation before making team-level calls; takes back decisions from people they delegated to as soon as the work gets hard.

name: People Development
definition: Invests in the growth of others through specific, timely feedback and deliberate development opportunities. Has the hard conversations early rather than letting performance issues fester, and tailors development to each individual's motivations and gaps. Treats developing others as part of own work, not as time taken away from it.
high: Gives specific developmental feedback timely enough for the person to act on it; spends 1:1 time on the person's development, not just on work-in-progress.
low: Lets developmental feedback drift to the formal review cycle; avoids difficult conversations until they become urgent or someone else has to step in.
